title: Cask & Copper — Single Malt Heritage Launch
description: A split-canvas keynote slide anchored by a side-lit amber bottle on deep walnut ground, with a copperplate-serif wordmark and a single italic brand story sentence. It carries Macallan-grade gravitas without relying on ornament or excess.
philosophy: This design exists for brands that speak through restraint. It refuses gradient noise, crowded layouts, and sans-serif utility — trusting instead that a perfectly lit bottle on a walnut-dark field communicates more than a dozen slide elements ever could. The copperplate wordmark is intentionally modest: heritage needs no announcement, only presence. It is made for boardrooms, private tastings, and investor suites where the product does all the persuading.
goodFor: Heritage spirits brand keynotes and single-product launch decks
Luxury goods reveals built around one cinematic hero photograph
Premium investor presentations for estate distilleries or heritage consumer brands
Award ceremony title slides for prestige food-and-drink events
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial reviews requiring dense data grids
High-energy consumer-tech launches expecting vivid color and motion
Multi-SKU catalog slides needing rows of product images
Academic or research decks requiring extended readable body-text columns
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a dimly lit private tasting room — one raking light source catches the shoulder of an amber bottle against deep walnut darkness, and nothing else competes for attention. Composition is asymmetric and unhurried: cinematic photograph commanding the left in near-silence, a sparse engraved wordmark breathing in studied isolation on the right. Mood draws from heritage editorial restraint — confident, shadow-rich, and slow. Avoid decorative ornament, gradient noise, or any element that crowds the essential tension between warm highlight and deep field.

examples.layoutNotes: The canvas splits roughly 55/45 — the left panel is a full-bleed photographic fill of the side-lit bottle against walnut-dark ground, bleeding to all three outer edges; the right panel is a text column occupying cols 7–11 of a 12-col grid with an 8% inner margin flanking the gutter. The wordmark sits at vertical center of the right panel, anchored below by a single hairline rule that separates it from one italic brand-story sentence. No header band is present; a discreet slide counter appears at the bottom-right corner of the text panel only.

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the hush of a private tasting room — dimly lit, deliberate, every element chosen rather than placed. Compositional rhythm is sparse-vertical: three quiet content units breathing inside luxurious negative space, as though each deserves a beat of silence before the next arrives. The mood is estate-aged gravitas, evoking the restraint of a handwritten whisky tasting note rather than a product advertisement. Avoid decorative flourishes, crowded groupings, or any visual element that competes with the content's own unhurried authority.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#1f1810"/>

  <!-- Subtle vignette using palette-only overlays -->
  <radialGradient id="vg" cx="50%" cy="45%" r="75%">
    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7a6a52" stop-opacity="0.08"/>
    <stop offset="70%" stop-color="#1f1810" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1f1810" stop-opacity="0.6"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="url(#vg)"/>

  <!-- Left gutter band (cols 1–2): hairline vertical rule -->
  <line x1="260" y1="150" x2="260" y2="930" stroke="#c9a55a" stroke-width="1" stroke-opacity="0.85"/>
  <circle cx="260" cy="150" r="2.5" fill="#c9a55a"/>
  <circle cx="260" cy="930" r="2.5" fill="#c9a55a"/>

  <!-- Discreet top wordmark, modest (aligned with content zone) -->
  <g transform="translate(480,150)">
    <text x="0" y="0" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="18" letter-spacing="8" fill="#7a6a52">CASK & COPPER</text>

  </g>

  <!-- Content zone (cols 3–10) -->

    <!-- Micro-label category header -->

    <!-- Primary restrained stat / statement -->
    <g transform="translate(0,170)">
      <text x="0" y="0" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="104" font-weight="400" fill="#f4ead2" letter-spacing="-1">
        Twenty-three winters
      </text>
      <text x="0" y="108" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="104" font-weight="400" fill="#f4ead2" letter-spacing="-1">
        in a single oloroso cask,
      </text>

      </text>
    </g>

    <!-- Attribution / sub-label -->
    <g transform="translate(0,730)">

  <!-- Folio number, anchored bottom-right in outer margin -->
  <g transform="translate(1780,990)">
    <text text-anchor="end" x="0" y="0" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="14" letter-spacing="4" fill="#7a6a52">FOLIO</text>
    <text text-anchor="end" x="0" y="28" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="22" fill="#c9a55a">07 / 24</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Minimal accent mark bottom-left to echo the copper rule -->
  <line x1="260" y1="990" x2="300" y2="990" stroke="#c9a55a" stroke-width="1"/>

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a narrow left gutter band (cols 1–2) holding a hairline vertical rule in an aged-copper accent tone, visually separating it from the primary content zone spanning cols 3–10, with cols 11–12 left as a breathing outer margin. The content zone stacks no more than three discrete typographic units — a micro-label category header, a primary statement or restrained stat callout, and an attribution or sub-label line — each separated by generous vertical rhythm rather than dividers or icon rows. A slim horizontal rule immediately beneath the category header provides hierarchy through geometry alone, not weight contrast. Folio number anchors bottom-right in the outer margin; no top header band, no decorative border frame.
